text:
sara: Quick design q — we're sketching envelope encryption for multi-cloud (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault). Two specific asks: 1) how often should the inference path call KMS to unwrap DEKs (latency-sensitive), and 2) what RBAC + audit signals do we need to support live rotations/incident response?

matt: TL;DR: avoid per-request KMS calls. Cache plaintext DEKs in secure in-memory cache with a conservative TTL (5–15m) and add explicit invalidation hooks for rotation/compromise. Keep KMS calls for: initial GenerateDataKey, cache misses, explicit rewrap/rotation, and emergency unwrap on recovery.

jin: For cloud differences — AWS GenerateDataKey is cheap but still ~10s-100s ms depending on region. GCP/CryptoKeyVersions has similar variability. So design for local cache + async renewers. Also consider using per-region KMS endpoints to reduce latency.

matt: Example config snippet we've used internally:```yaml
encryption:
  dek_cache:
    ttl_seconds: 600    # 10m - tuned per workload
    max_entries: 2000
    eviction_policy: LRU
    secure_mlock: true   # mlock pages, don't swap
  rewrap:
    strategy: async_stream  # stream rewraps off main path
    batch_size: 500
    backoff_ms: 200
```

ethan: RBAC notes: create narrowly scoped roles per runtime tier. Example roles: `kms-dek-unwrapper` (can Decrypt/DecryptDataKey), `kms-key-admin` (rotate/disable keys), `kms-rewrap-runner` (encrypt with new KEK). Use short-lived creds for runtimes (STS / Workload Identity) so revocation is faster.

maria: Audit signals we should capture in logs (and push to SIEM): `request_id`, `principal`, `operation` (GenerateDataKey/Encrypt/Decrypt), `key_id`, `key_version`, `tenant_id`, `route` (service/instance), and a fingerprint of the ciphertext (sha256 prefix). Cloud audit logs + application-level logs for correlation. Make sure to include the rewrap job's job_id and input DEK metadata.

sara: For rotation/incident flow — how to rewrap millions of DEKs without killing latency?

maria: Staged rewrap: mark new KEK version in metadata (object header `kek_version`). New writes use new KEK. Existing objects keep old kek_version. Kick an async rewrap pipeline that streams objects (snapshot -> rewrap -> commit) with backpressure. Offer a read-time fallback: if unwrap with current KEK fails, try previous KEK(s) for a bounded window (24–72h). That avoids fail-open for reads during migration.

jin: Implementation optimization: store DEK wrapped_by_kek_version and wrapped_ciphertext. Rewrap job calls KMS only for Encrypt(plaintext_DEK) after locally decrypting using cached DEK if available, otherwise call KMS Decrypt once per object during rewrap. To reduce KMS calls, use streaming rewrap that operates on batches and reuses decrypted DEK for multiple operations when applicable.

matt: Emergency revocation: rotate KEK (disable old in KMS), then run rewrap for high-risk tenants first. For immediate block: revoke the `kms-dek-unwrapper` role for affected service accounts and invalidate local DEK caches (send invalidation via pub/sub so all instances flush).

security-bot: Reminder: plaintext DEKs must never be persisted. Zeroize memory after use, use mlock where possible, and ensure crash dumps cannot include keys. Also add test coverage for memory wipe on GC/eviction. :lock: :warning:

ethan: Audit/Alerting rules ideas: alert on abnormal KMS Decrypt rate per principal (spike could indicate exfil), alert on rewrap job failure rate > 1% per hour, and on any Decrypt operations for KEKs marked compromised.

maria: Also consider per-tenant KEKs for high-compliance customers so rotation/compromise scopes are limited. That increases KMS quota usage but simplifies compliance boundaries.

sara: Great — plan: prototype with 10m TTL, secure in-memory cache, async rewraper, and add an invalidate pub/sub channel + RBAC role `kms-dek-unwrapper`. I'll draft a runbook for rotation + incident steps. Thanks y'all. :pray:
